# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations

- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

1 | # docugate
2 | 
3 | Command-line tools for [DocuGate](https://www.trydocugate.site), which publishes
4 | documentation straight from the markdown in your GitHub repositories and decides
5 | who may read it.
6 | 
7 | ```sh
8 | npm i -g docugate
9 | ```
10 | 
11 | ```sh
12 | docugate init     # set this repository up for DocuGate
13 | docugate check    # check the docs the way DocuGate will read them
14 | docugate openapi  # prepare an OpenAPI spec for the API reference
15 | ```
16 | 
17 | Installing the command once is usually simpler than reaching for a package
18 | manager in each repository: it needs no `package.json`, so it works just as
19 | well in a Go, Python or Flutter repository as in a JavaScript one. That matters
20 | because one DocuGate space can read from several repositories, and they are
21 | rarely all the same language.
22 | 
23 | If you would rather not install it globally, `npm i -D docugate` adds it to a
24 | single Node project, which also pins the version for CI; `npx docugate` runs it
25 | without installing anything. Both work with pnpm, yarn and bun too.
26 | 
27 | Requires Node 18.17 or later. Run every command from the root of your
28 | repository.
29 | 
30 | 
31 | ## IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon
32 | 
33 | This repository is DocuGate's entry to the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon (lablab.ai,
34 | September 25 to 27, 2026). To be clear about what was built when:
35 | 
36 | * **Before the event:** the CLI above (`init`, `check`, `openapi`), moved here
37 |   from DocuGate's private repository with its history.
38 | * **During the event, with IBM Bob:** the UI tour: the `.docugate/tour/` format,
39 |   `docugate tour serve`, tour checks in `docugate check`, and the pill with its
40 |   inspector. Screenshots of the Bob sessions are in `bob_sessions/`.
41 | * **During the event, without Bob:** `docugate tour init`, which installs the
42 |   Tour Writer mode and runs IBM Bob through Bob Shell to write an app's first
43 |   tour, and the demo app, [Ledgerly](https://github.com/Docugate/docugate-demo).
44 | 
45 | ## Several repositories in one space
46 | 
47 | A space can merge the docs from a frontend, a backend and a mobile app into one
48 | set of pages, so a feature that spans all three is documented once instead of
49 | three times. Repositories are added to a space from its settings on
50 | [trydocugate.site](https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard), not from here.
51 | 
52 | What that changes for this package: run `init` and `check` in **each**
53 | repository that contributes docs. Every one gets its own `docugate.json`, naming
54 | its own docs folder. `check` reads the repository it is run in, which is why its
55 | 300-page limit is per repository rather than per space.
56 | 
57 | See [Merging repositories](https://www.trydocugate.site/docs/merging-repositories).
58 | 
59 | ## `init`
60 | 
61 | Creates a `docugate.json` and, if your docs folder has no markdown yet, a first
62 | `index.md`. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run in a repository
63 | that already has docs.
64 | 
65 | ```sh
66 | docugate init --dir docs --title "Acme API"
67 | ```
68 | 
69 | Then push, and publish the space from your
70 | [DocuGate dashboard](https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard/new).
71 | 
72 | ## `check`
73 | 
74 | Reads your docs folder with DocuGate's own rules and reports what the
75 | published page would get wrong:
76 | 
77 | - **Errors:** broken links between pages, links that leave the docs folder,
78 |   two files that become the same URL, an unreadable `docugate.json`, an empty
79 |   docs folder, or more than 300 pages.
80 | - **Warnings:** pages with no `# Title`, front matter, `.mdx` files, no landing
81 |   page, and `sidebar` entries that match nothing.
82 | 
83 | It exits with 1 when there are errors (add `--strict` to fail on warnings too),
84 | so it works as a CI step:
85 | 
86 | ```yaml
87 | # .github/workflows/docs.yml
88 | name: Docs
89 | on: [push, pull_request]
90 | jobs:
91 |   check:
92 |     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
93 |     steps:
94 |       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
95 |       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
96 |         with:
97 |           node-version: 22
98 |       - run: npx docugate@0.1 check
99 | ```

102 | it from there. Without a pin, the rules being enforced can change between two
103 | runs of the same workflow, which turns a green build red with nothing in the
104 | commit to explain it.

106 | ## `openapi`
107 | 
108 | Takes the OpenAPI 3 spec your backend already produces and writes the version
109 | you want published: only the public paths, without sensitive fields, with keys
110 | in a stable order so it reviews cleanly in a pull request.
111 | 
112 | ```sh
113 | docugate openapi --from http://localhost:3000/openapi.json \
114 |   --exclude "/internal/**" --redact passwordHash --out openapi.json
115 | ```
116 | 
117 | - `--from`: a `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml` file, or a URL serving one.
118 | - `--include` / `--exclude`: path globs; `*` matches within one segment and
119 |   `**` matches across segments. Both can be repeated.
120 | - `--redact`: a property name to remove from every schema and example.

126 | `docugate.json`:

# docugate

DocuGate publishes documentation straight from the markdown in your GitHub repositories and shows a walkthrough pill on your running app so any developer can see what each element on screen is and where its data comes from.

```sh
npm i -g docugate
```

---

## Quick start

`cd` into your app's repository, then run:

```sh
docugate init
```

It walks you through four steps:

1. **Repository role.** Say whether this repository is the frontend, the backend, or both.
2. **Sign in and connect.** Sign in to DocuGate with GitHub and connect this repository to a space.
3. **IBM Bob writes the tour.** Bob reads the code and writes one `.docugate/tour/*.md` file for each screen it finds.
4. **The pill is added to your app.** The dev-only loader snippet is inserted into your HTML or layout file.

Once that is done:

```sh
docugate tour serve
```

Start your app in another terminal, open it in the browser, and the pill appears in the corner.

---

## Tours

A tour helps a developer who is new to a codebase see what each element on screen is and where its data comes from. For each screen there is one markdown file in `.docugate/tour/`. Each file has front matter with a `route` and a `title`, then one `##` section per stop.

**Example stop:**

```markdown
---
route: /invoices/:id
title: Invoice detail
---

## Total
target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
source: backend/src/billing.ts
docs: https://example.com/docs/billing

The amount due: the subtotal plus tax, computed by `totals()` in the backend.
```

Fields:

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | yes | CSS selector for the element. Prefer `[data-tour="…"]`. |
| `data` | no | Request and field: `METHOD /path → field`. |
| `code` | yes | File that renders the element, relative to the repository root. |
| `source` | no | File where the value is computed, when that is elsewhere. |
| `docs` | no | URL to relevant documentation. |

The prose paragraph after the fields explains what the element is and why its value is what it is.

Tour files are yours. `docugate tour init` never overwrites a file that already exists.

---

## The pill

When `docugate tour serve` is running, the pill appears in the corner of your app. It has two modes:

- **Walkthrough.** Steps through every stop on the current screen in order, highlighting each element and showing its tour card.
- **Inspector.** Hover over any element to see its stop. Elements that have no stop yet show an **Add to tour** form so you can write one from the browser and save it directly to the tour file.

The pill only loads when the tour server is reachable at `localhost`. It never shows in production.

---

## Keeping tours true

`docugate check` reads your docs folder with DocuGate's own rules and also checks every tour file:

- **Errors:** broken links between pages, two files that become the same URL, an empty docs folder, more than 300 pages, a tour stop with a missing `target` or `code` field.
- **Warnings:** pages with no `# Title`, front matter, `.mdx` files, no landing page.

It exits with code 1 when there are errors. Add `--strict` to also fail on warnings.

Use it in CI:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docs.yml
name: Docs
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - run: npx docugate@latest check --strict
```

---

## Commands

| Command | Main flags | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docugate init` | `--dir`, `--title`, `--role frontend\|backend\|both`, `--yes` | Set up this repository for DocuGate (interactive). |
| `docugate check` | `--dir`, `--strict` | Check docs and tour files the way DocuGate will read them. |
| `docugate openapi` | `--from`, `--out`, `--include`, `--exclude`, `--redact`, `--check` | Prepare an OpenAPI spec for the API reference. |
| `docugate login` | | Sign in to DocuGate with GitHub. |
| `docugate logout` | | Sign out and delete saved credentials. |
| `docugate whoami` | | Print the currently signed-in user. |
| `docugate tour init` | `--max-cost <n>`, `--team-id <id>` | Write the first tour with IBM Bob (uses Bob Shell). |
| `docugate tour serve` | `--port <n>` (default 4178) | Start the local server that serves tour data for the pill. |
| `docugate tour install` | `--port <n>`, `--remove` | Add (or remove) the pill loader from your app's HTML or layout. |
| `docugate tour export <file>` | | Write every tour screen to a single JSON file. |

Run every command from the root of your repository.

---

## Try it on the demo

Clone [docugate-demo](https://github.com/Docugate/docugate-demo), a small full-stack app with a pre-written tour:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Docugate/docugate-demo
cd docugate-demo

# install dependencies and start the app
npm install
npm run dev
```

In a second terminal:

```sh
cd docugate-demo
docugate tour serve
```

Open the app in the browser. The pill appears in the bottom-right corner.

---

## Several repositories in one space

A space can merge docs from a frontend, a backend, and a mobile app into one set of pages. Repositories are added to a space from its settings on [trydocugate.site](https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard), not from here.

Run `init` and `check` in each repository that contributes docs. Every one gets its own `docugate.json`, naming its own docs folder. `check` reads the repository it is run in, which is why its 300-page limit is per repository rather than per space.

See [Merging repositories](https://www.trydocugate.site/docs/merging-repositories).

---

## `openapi`

Takes the OpenAPI 3 spec your backend already produces and writes the version you want published: only the public paths, without sensitive fields, with keys in a stable order so it reviews cleanly in a pull request.

```sh
docugate openapi --from http://localhost:3000/openapi.json \
  --exclude "/internal/**" --redact passwordHash --out openapi.json
```

- `--from`: a `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml` file, or a URL serving one.
- `--include` / `--exclude`: path globs; `*` matches within one segment and `**` matches across segments. Both can be repeated.
- `--redact`: a property name to remove from every schema and example. Can be repeated.
- `--check`: do not write anything; exit with 1 if the committed file is out of date. Useful in CI.

Instead of passing flags every time, set the same options in `docugate.json`:

```json
{
  "docsDir": "docs",
  "api": {
    "generate": {
      "from": "http://localhost:3000/openapi.json",
      "output": "openapi.json",
      "exclude": ["/internal/**"],
      "redact": ["passwordHash"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## `docugate.json`

One per repository, at its root.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `docsDir` | The folder DocuGate reads. Defaults to `docs`. |
| `title` | The space's title. |
| `role` | Repository role: `frontend`, `backend`, or `both`. Set by `docugate init`. |
| `sidebar` | File and folder names in the order the sidebar should show them. Orders this repository's own pages, not the whole space. |
| `api.generate` | Defaults for `docugate openapi`. |

---

## IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon

This repository is DocuGate's entry to the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon (lablab.ai, September 25 to 27, 2026). To be clear about what was built when:

**Before the event:** the CLI that was already in DocuGate's private repository: `docugate init`, `docugate check`, and `docugate openapi`. Moved here with its history.

**During the event, with IBM Bob** (tasks in `bob_sessions/`):

- **Task 01** — first tour: the `.docugate/tour/` file format, `parseTourFile`, `loadTours`, and the stop schema.
- **Task 02** — tour checks: `docugate check` extended to validate tour files (missing `target`, missing `code`).
- **Task 03** — `docugate tour serve`: the local HTTP server that serves tour data and SSE change events to the pill, plus `docugate tour export`.
- **Task 04** — the pill: the `DocugatePill` web component, the walkthrough, the inspector, and the Add to tour form.
- **Task 05** — one-command init: `docugate tour install`, the `docugate init` interactive flow with role selection and pill installation, and the hint in `docugate tour serve`.
- **Task 06** — login: `docugate login`, `docugate logout`, `docugate whoami`, the GitHub OAuth callback flow, and connecting a repository to a space during `docugate init`.

`docugate tour init` itself runs IBM Bob through Bob Shell (`bob run --mode tour-writer …`). It installs a Tour Writer custom mode into `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` with file-edit permissions scoped to `.docugate/tour/`, then hands the codebase to Bob and puts back any file Bob changed that the user had already written.

---

## Licence

MIT

## Quick start

`cd` into your app's repository, then run:

```sh
docugate init
```

It walks you through four steps:

1. **Repository role.** Say whether this repository is the frontend, the backend, or both.
2. **Sign in and connect.** Sign in to DocuGate with GitHub and connect this repository to a space.
3. **IBM Bob writes the tour.** Bob reads the code and writes one `.docugate/tour/*.md` file for each screen it finds.
4. **The pill is added to your app.** The dev-only loader snippet is inserted into your HTML or layout file.

Once that is done:

```sh
docugate tour serve
```

Start your app in another terminal, open it in the browser, and the pill appears in the corner.

---

## Tours

A tour helps a developer who is new to a codebase see what each element on screen is and where its data comes from. For each screen there is one markdown file in `.docugate/tour/`. Each file has front matter with a `route` and a `title`, then one `##` section per stop.

**Example stop:**

```markdown
---
route: /invoices/:id
title: Invoice detail
---

## Total
target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
source: backend/src/billing.ts
docs: https://example.com/docs/billing

```

Fields:

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | yes | CSS selector for the element. Prefer `[data-tour="…"]`. |
| `data` | no | Request and field: `METHOD /path → field`. |
| `code` | yes | File that renders the element, relative to the repository root. |
| `source` | no | File where the value is computed, when that is elsewhere. |
| `docs` | no | URL to relevant documentation. |

The prose paragraph after the fields explains what the element is and why its value is what it is.

Tour files are yours. `docugate tour init` never overwrites a file that already exists.

---

## The pill

When `docugate tour serve` is running, the pill appears in the corner of your app. It has two modes:

- **Walkthrough.** Steps through every stop on the current screen in order, highlighting each element and showing its tour card.
- **Inspector.** Hover over any element to see its stop. Elements that have no stop yet show an **Add to tour** form so you can write one from the browser and save it directly to the tour file.

The pill only loads when the tour server is reachable at `localhost`. It never shows in production.

---

## Keeping tours true

`docugate check` reads your docs folder with DocuGate's own rules and also checks every tour file:

- **Errors:** broken links between pages, two files that become the same URL, an empty docs folder, more than 300 pages, a tour stop with a missing `target` or `code` field.
- **Warnings:** pages with no `# Title`, front matter, `.mdx` files, no landing page.

It exits with code 1 when there are errors. Add `--strict` to also fail on warnings.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/docs.yml
name: Docs
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4

      - run: npx docugate@latest check --strict
```

+# docugate
+
+DocuGate publishes documentation straight from the markdown in your GitHub repositories and shows a walkthrough pill on your running app so any developer can see what each element on screen is and where its data comes from.
+
+```sh
+npm i -g docugate
+```
+
+---
+
+## Quick start
+
+`cd` into your app's repository, then run:
+
+```sh
+docugate init
+```
+
+It walks you through four steps:
+
+1. **Repository role.** Say whether this repository is the frontend, the backend, or both.
+2. **Sign in and connect.** Sign in to DocuGate with GitHub and connect this repository to a space.
+3. **IBM Bob writes the tour.** Bob reads the code and writes one `.docugate/tour/*.md` file for each screen it finds.
+4. **The pill is added to your app.** The dev-only loader snippet is inserted into your HTML or layout file.
+
+Once that is done:
+
+```sh
+docugate tour serve
+```
+
+Start your app in another terminal, open it in the browser, and the pill appears in the corner.
+
+---
+
+## Tours
+
+A tour helps a developer who is new to a codebase see what each element on screen is and where its data comes from. For each screen there is one markdown file in `.docugate/tour/`. Each file has front matter with a `route` and a `title`, then one `##` section per stop.
+
+**Example stop:**
+
+```markdown
+---
+route: /invoices/:id
+title: Invoice detail
+---
+
+## Total
+target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
+data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
+code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
+source: backend/src/billing.ts
+docs: https://example.com/docs/billing
+
+The amount due: the subtotal plus tax, computed by `totals()` in the backend.
+```
+
+Fields:
+
+| Field | Required | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `target` | yes | CSS selector for the element. Prefer `[data-tour="…"]`. |
+| `data` | no | Request and field: `METHOD /path → field`. |
+| `code` | yes | File that renders the element, relative to the repository root. |
+| `source` | no | File where the value is computed, when that is elsewhere. |
+| `docs` | no | URL to relevant documentation. |
+
+The prose paragraph after the fields explains what the element is and why its value is what it is.
+
+Tour files are yours. `docugate tour init` never overwrites a file that already exists.
+
+---
+
+## The pill
+
+When `docugate tour serve` is running, the pill appears in the corner of your app. It has two modes:
+
+- **Walkthrough.** Steps through every stop on the current screen in order, highlighting each element and showing its tour card.
+- **Inspector.** Hover over any element to see its stop. Elements that have no stop yet show an **Add to tour** form so you can write one from the browser and save it directly to the tour file.
+
+The pill only loads when the tour server is reachable at `localhost`. It never shows in production.
+
+---
+
+## Keeping tours true
+
+`docugate check` reads your docs folder with DocuGate's own rules and also checks every tour file:
+
+- **Errors:** broken links between pages, two files that become the same URL, an empty docs folder, more than 300 pages, a tour stop with a missing `target` or `code` field.
+- **Warnings:** pages with no `# Title`, front matter, `.mdx` files, no landing page.
+
+It exits with code 1 when there are errors. Add `--strict` to also fail on warnings.
+
+Use it in CI:
+
+```yaml
+# .github/workflows/docs.yml
+name: Docs
+on: [push, pull_request]
+jobs:
+  check:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+      - run: npx docugate@latest check --strict
+```
+
+---
+
+## Commands
+
+| Command | Main flags | What it does |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `docugate init` | `--dir`, `--title`, `--role frontend\|backend\|both`, `--yes` | Set up this repository for DocuGate (interactive). |
+| `docugate check` | `--dir`, `--strict` | Check docs and tour files the way DocuGate will read them. |
+| `docugate openapi` | `--from`, `--out`, `--include`, `--exclude`, `--redact`, `--check` | Prepare an OpenAPI spec for the API reference. |
+| `docugate login` | | Sign in to DocuGate with GitHub. |
+| `docugate logout` | | Sign out and delete saved credentials. |
+| `docugate whoami` | | Print the currently signed-in user. |
+| `docugate tour init` | `--max-cost <n>`, `--team-id <id>` | Write the first tour with IBM Bob (uses Bob Shell). |
+| `docugate tour serve` | `--port <n>` (default 4178) | Start the local server that serves tour data for the pill. |
+| `docugate tour install` | `--port <n>`, `--remove` | Add (or remove) the pill loader from your app's HTML or layout. |
+| `docugate tour export <file>` | | Write every tour screen to a single JSON file. |
+
+Run every command from the root of your repository.
+
+---
+
+## Try it on the demo
+
+Clone [docugate-demo](https://github.com/Docugate/docugate-demo), a small full-stack app with a pre-written tour:
+
+```sh
+git clone https://github.com/Docugate/docugate-demo
+cd docugate-demo
+
+# install dependencies and start the app
+npm install
+npm run dev
+```
+
+In a second terminal:
+
+```sh
+cd docugate-demo
+docugate tour serve
+```
+
+Open the app in the browser. The pill appears in the bottom-right corner.
+
+---
+
+## Several repositories in one space
+
+A space can merge docs from a frontend, a backend, and a mobile app into one set of pages. Repositories are added to a space from its settings on [trydocugate.site](https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard), not from here.
+
+Run `init` and `check` in each repository that contributes docs. Every one gets its own `docugate.json`, naming its own docs folder. `check` reads the repository it is run in, which is why its 300-page limit is per repository rather than per space.
+
+See [Merging repositories](https://www.trydocugate.site/docs/merging-repositories).
+
+---
+
+## `openapi`
+
+Takes the OpenAPI 3 spec your backend already produces and writes the version you want published: only the public paths, without sensitive fields, with keys in a stable order so it reviews cleanly in a pull request.
+
+```sh
+docugate openapi --from http://localhost:3000/openapi.json \
+  --exclude "/internal/**" --redact passwordHash --out openapi.json
+```
+
+- `--from`: a `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml` file, or a URL serving one.
+- `--include` / `--exclude`: path globs; `*` matches within one segment and `**` matches across segments. Both can be repeated.
+- `--redact`: a property name to remove from every schema and example. Can be repeated.
+- `--check`: do not write anything; exit with 1 if the committed file is out of date. Useful in CI.
+
+Instead of passing flags every time, set the same options in `docugate.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "docsDir": "docs",
+  "api": {
+    "generate": {
+      "from": "http://localhost:3000/openapi.json",
+      "output": "openapi.json",
+      "exclude": ["/internal/**"],
+      "redact": ["passwordHash"]
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+---
+
+## `docugate.json`
+
+One per repository, at its root.
+
+| Key | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `docsDir` | The folder DocuGate reads. Defaults to `docs`. |
+| `title` | The space's title. |
+| `role` | Repository role: `frontend`, `backend`, or `both`. Set by `docugate init`. |
+| `sidebar` | File and folder names in the order the sidebar should show them. Orders this repository's own pages, not the whole space. |
+| `api.generate` | Defaults for `docugate openapi`. |
+
+---
+
+## IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon
+
+This repository is DocuGate's entry to the IBM Bob 2.0 hackathon (lablab.ai, September 25 to 27, 2026). To be clear about what was built when:
+
+**Before the event:** the CLI that was already in DocuGate's private repository: `docugate init`, `docugate check`, and `docugate openapi`. Moved here with its history.
+
+**During the event, with IBM Bob** (tasks in `bob_sessions/`):
+
+- **Task 01** — first tour: the `.docugate/tour/` file format, `parseTourFile`, `loadTours`, and the stop schema.
+- **Task 02** — tour checks: `docugate check` extended to validate tour files (missing `target`, missing `code`).
+- **Task 03** — `docugate tour serve`: the local HTTP server that serves tour data and SSE change events to the pill, plus `docugate tour export`.
+- **Task 04** — the pill: the `DocugatePill` web component, the walkthrough, the inspector, and the Add to tour form.
+- **Task 05** — one-command init: `docugate tour install`, the `docugate init` interactive flow with role selection and pill installation, and the hint in `docugate tour serve`.
+- **Task 06** — login: `docugate login`, `docugate logout`, `docugate whoami`, the GitHub OAuth callback flow, and connecting a repository to a space during `docugate init`.
+
+`docugate tour init` itself runs IBM Bob through Bob Shell (`bob run --mode tour-writer …`). It installs a Tour Writer custom mode into `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` with file-edit permissions scoped to `.docugate/tour/`, then hands the codebase to Bob and puts back any file Bob changed that the user had already written.
